title: Result
description: The terminal result record a worker writes once to the result store under the job's `result_key`, and the coordinator reads to answer GET /jobs/{id} (protocols.md §2). Shape mirrors an OpenAI completion plus the clusterbuck envelope {status, error, worker}.

job_id.description: The id of the job this result belongs to.

status.description: Terminal state only. Non-terminal (queued/running) is queue state, assembled by the server, never stored here.

worker.description: Opaque node id of the worker that ran the job (diagnostics only; the client never learns the physical machine).

started_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp immediately BEFORE the executor called the model server. With `finished_at` this is the actual inference duration, measured where it happens. OPTIONAL because not every terminal result comes from an executor: the coordinator writes its own for a dead-lettered, expired or cancelled job, and those never called a model, so there is no honest value to supply.

finished_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp immediately AFTER the model server returned (or failed). Optional for the same reason as `started_at`; an executor that reports one reports both.

completed_at.description: DEPRECATED, and never meant what its name says: it was stamped BEFORE inference, so it is a processing-START time, wrong by a full inference duration. Retained for one release equal to `started_at` so no existing reader silently changes meaning; read `started_at`/`finished_at` instead.

completion.description: OpenAI-style chat completion on success; null on failure/expiry. additionalProperties allowed so the model server's native fields pass through.

error.description: Failure detail when status != done; null on success.

usage.description: Token accounting, when the model server reports it.
